To understand something, you have to stand under it.

Kevin Trudeau explains what prostrating really means in this ancient teaching. It is not always falling at someone's feet. It is mostly an attitude of humility: you feel you don't know that much, and you trust the teacher knows a little more.

He says you place yourself below the teacher and you receive, because receiving knowledge is only possible if you can humble yourself.

Where in your life could a little humility open a door?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

Think you're equal to your teacher? The flow stops.

Kevin Trudeau uses a simple picture. One empty beaker and one full of water are joined by a siphon tube. The water only flows while the empty beaker sits below the full one.

If the receiver says, "I should be equal to you," the flow stops. His point: a humble, empty mind can receive, and pride shuts the flow off.

Are you holding yourself above the people you could learn from?

#ad #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

The best teacher in the world can't help a closed student.

Kevin Trudeau says you are the receiver and the teacher is the transmitter. Humility is what allows you to receive.

He adds that it is the teacher's job to convince the student. If that never happens, maybe this teacher is not the right one for that person. Either way, the student has to be willing to listen.

What would change if you listened first?

#ad #mindset #success #kevintrudeau
